First things first, I would like to point out that /v/snaxchange is not the only snack exchange thread on Voat, but it is the most alive. I hope to help make snaxchange the snack trading sub, and your input is key here.

Secondly, a bit about myself. I have used Voat since May 2015, and Reddit since early 2014. My account @Netfang is dedicated to this sub. IRL, I live in Idaho for the time being.

I have spent years buying and selling things online out of my house, as a mix between a hobby and a source of income. I also work part time in shipping, so I have experience in helping things survive the mail system.

I also like to try new foods, which is why I've created the sub. An Icelandic Redditor sent me some very salty Opal licorice, I've had the chance to try Vegemite (it's good in small quantities, I promise!) and I love Canada's own Coffee Crisp.

I believe it is important to supply any of you potential traders with some tips. I'd also like to give kudos to these folks for their useful tidbits posted over the years...which I've used as an inspiration for my own pointers.

Conducting a smooth exchange

Creating your post:

Creating a post is a very important first step, and of course, your post will start with a title. In your title BE SURE to include the location you'll be shipping from. In the future I hope to add a flag feature; for now, do add the location to the title. If you know what foods you want to send or receive, it will be helpful to add these to your title as well. Of course you may want to do some shopping around first, so use discretion when writing the title. For example, a title I might write would look like this:

ID, USA: Have Potatoes, looking for Belgian Chocolate

or

USA, Idaho, Looking for a taste of Singapore

Planning the transaction:

When you think you've found a trading partner, be sure to browse their profile. According to /r/snackexchange around 95% of trades are completed, but most of the bad trades involve new accounts with low combined CCP/SCP. Even if the account you are looking at seems established, use your discretion--use your gut feeling--before spending money on an internet stranger.

PLEASE REMEMBER that by trading you have NO GUARANTEE OF RECEIVING A PACKAGE. While I am not advising illegal activities here on Voat, I can not make any guarantees as to your safety, money, taste in food, or taste in trading partners. I will work to combat scammers as they appear, but I will not compensate you for your loss.

If you were not already planning on doing this: make sure to tell your partner if there is something you cannot consume. Regardless if this is for personal reasons, religious guidelines, or cultural standards, it is your responsibility to advocate for yourself.

Finally, trading on /v/snaxchange does not require an IRL identity, for our friends in Guy Fawkes masks, so don't be pushy about it. Keep in mind that your trading partner can be entirely serious about trading with you and using a fake name. All mail from me will have Netfang on the return address. If you require a last name for customs forms or another reason, you can always use Voat or make one up.

Preparing the package:

Make sure you are able to send your intended snacks. International shipping and food can be complicated depending on what you've decided to send. A great way to find out what you can and cannot send is to search for the destination country and customs regulations, ie "Canada shipping regulations" where official government sites will often have notes about food products. If you send something against the rules, you will run the risk of your partner receiving nothing in the mail. Lousy!

Packaging is very important! Hopefully you will have some intuition as to how to send your goodies, but remember that, irrespective of what you'll be shipping, the contents should not be able to move freely in the package. If you are feeling adventurous enough to send it, be very careful when mailing carbonated drinks, glass and flimsy wood. Remember that postmen may drop, toss, throw or even kick your package! If you are not sure how to mail something, search for help on the internet (you're on it right now! Hooray!) or don't mail it.

Do your best job when filling out customs, and remember that customs can open packages. If your items are confiscated, your best case scenario will involve your trading partner receiving no package. If you try to beat the system, the system could beat you instead.

Up until now everything has been focused on you doing a good job, but please note that not all couriers do a good job. Some services feature exorbitant fees, and some routinely steal packages. As with all things, the responsibility of sending a tasty package is on you, even if your package is stolen.

Be sure to send your trading partner photos of a postmarked package, and ask for them as well. By that point you will know that your exchangee is (most likely) a) serious about trading or (unlikely) b) trolling you so much that they've paid for postage and packaging. ^And ^that's ^dedication ^to ^trolling. If possible, ask for tracking numbers or a receipt picture.

Receiving the package:

What, it's not here yet? Do exercise patience. International mail is especially inconsistent in terms of time, but do wait up to six weeks for international packages before getting worried. Domestic packages (in the USA) can take multiple weeks as well, but use common sense and be patient. I once got a letter to Texas returned to me...5 months after sending it!

Finally, when you get your goodies, post pictures of them! You are not only providing free entertainment for the whole sub, but you are also giving your partner trading credibility. Do handwrite your exchangee's username for the photo, but be sure to black out any personal information in the photo.

TL;DR: Haha, this is too important for a TLDR. Besides, it took me a long time to write. Thanks for reading!
